facts.title: Symons Emergency Specialties, Inc. d/b/a Symbiosis
facts.agency: Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), VA Long Beach Healthcare System
facts.solicitation: Purchase order No. 36C26226P0525 (bridge order); RFQ No. 36C26225Q1093 (long-term requirement, resulting in IDIQ contract No. 36C26226D0030)
facts.procurement_type: Purchase order (short-term bridge) and IDIQ contract for non-emergent ambulance services
facts.protester: Symons Emergency Specialties, Inc. d/b/a Symbiosis (Symbiosis)
facts.awardee: EDG Entities LLC (EDG), a service-disabled veteran-owned small business
facts.background: The VA issued purchase order No. 36C26226P0525 to Symbiosis as a short-term bridge order for non-emergent ambulance services at the VA Long Beach Healthcare System. The bridge order was issued to prevent a break in services while litigation over the competitive procurement for the long-term requirement was pending. The VA later awarded IDIQ contract No. 36C26226D0030 to EDG under RFQ No. 36C26225Q1093 for the long-term requirement. The VA exercised an option to extend services under Symbiosis' purchase order. EDG then protested to GAO, arguing that the option could not be exercised because its price had not been evaluated when the order was awarded. In corrective action taken in response, the VA terminated the option under Symbiosis' purchase order. Symbiosis separately raised concerns about EDG's ongoing performance under the IDIQ contract.

protester_grounds.claim: The agency improperly terminated an option it had previously exercised under Symbiosis' purchase order.
EDG is not complying with the limitation on subcontracting requirements applicable to its IDIQ contract.
The entity actually performing the ambulance services under EDG's contract may lack the required licensing and regulatory authority in Los Angeles County.

facts.agency_position: The VA terminated the option as corrective action after determining that it should not have been exercised. The contracting officer stated that he did not evaluate the pricing for the option to extend services when the order was awarded to Symbiosis. The agency maintained that the termination was a proper contract administration decision.
facts.record_facts_protected: The contracting officer's statement says he did not evaluate the pricing for the option to extend services at the time of award to Symbiosis. The VA subsequently determined that this made exercise of the option improper. The long-term requirement was awarded to EDG, a service-disabled veteran-owned small business located in Long Beach, California. Symbiosis stated that it does not challenge EDG's evaluation or award and instead targets EDG's ongoing performance. The record does not show that the option was evaluated as part of the initial award.
